title: Combined Effects of Time Spent in Physical Activity, Sedentary Behaviors and Sleep on Obesity and Cardio-Metabolic Health Markers: A Novel Compositional Data Analysis Approach.
Data Source: NHANES
NonWear_Criterion: NR
Sleep_Detection_Method: "How much sleep do you actually get at night on weekdays or workdays" as integer from 1 to 24 hours
Cutpoint_Type: Standard count per minutes thresholds (Freedson et al, 1998)
Closure_Method: Sleep (self-report) and accelerometer-derived SB, LIPA, MVPA expressed as proportions of 24 h and normalized so the sum = 1
Outcome_Variable: BMI; waist circumference; systolic blood pressure; diastolic blood pressure; HDL; LDL; triglycerides; CRP; plasma glucose; plasma insulin; HOMA
Covariates: Age; Sex; Race/ethnicity; Marital status; Education; Work status; Ratio of family income to poverty level; Smoking status; Alcohol consumption; Caffeine intake; Total energy intake; Saturated fat intake; Self-reported health (SF-12); Previous diagnosis of cancer; Previous diagnosis of diabetes; Previous diagnosis of cardiovascular disease; Previous diagnosis of stroke; Current use of diabetic medication; Current use of antihypertensive medication; Current use of lipidemic medication
Stratified_Analyses: BMI; Waist circumference; Blood pressure; HDL; LDL; Triglycerides; Plasma glucose; Plasma insulin; HOMA categories
Sensitivity_Analyses: Removed 10% of cases at random to test stability of model estimates

title: Associations between sleep duration, sedentary time, physical activity, and health indicators among Canadian children and youth using compositional analyses.
Data Source: Canadian Health Measures Survey (CHMS) cycles 1 to 3
NonWear_Criterion: ³60 consecutive minutes of zero counts, with allowance for 2 min of counts between zero and 100
Sleep_Detection_Method: Self-reported (response to "How many hours do you (your child) usually spend sleeping in a 24-hour period, excluding time spent resting.")
Cutpoint_Type: Count per minutes thresholds (Colley et al. 2010)
Outcome_Variable: zBMI; Waist circumference; Blood pressure; Behavioural strengths and difficulties; Aerobic fitness; Triglycerides; High-density lipoprotein cholesterol; C-reactive protein; Insulin
Covariates: Age; Sex; Highest household education
Stratified_Analyses: BMI z-score groups; All other health indicators stratified by quartiles
Bootstrap: Used to estimate standard errors and coefficients of variation to account for survey design effects)

title: Adiposity and the isotemporal substitution of physical activity, sedentary time and sleep among school-aged children: a compositional data analysis approach.
Data Source: International Study of Childhood Obesity, Lifestyle and the Environment (ISCOLE)
NonWear_Criterion: ³20 consecutive minutes of 0 activity counts
Sleep_Detection_Method: Fully automated algorithm (ActiLife software)
Covariates: Highest education level of either parent; Number of parents in the home; Number of siblings in the home
Main_Findings: Reallocating time from MVPA to other behaviors unfavorably impacts body fat%; the compositional model is preferred over the traditional model as its estimates correctly account for the asymmetry, non-linearity, and starting activity composition of the child.

title: Compositional associations of time spent in sleep, sedentary behavior and physical activity with obesity measures in children.
Data Source: Primary data collection (Kingston, Canada)
NonWear_Criterion: ³60 min of 0 counts (allow 2 min <100 counts)
Sleep_Detection_Method: Log-Based (Derived from Actical + sleep log verified visually against accelerometer data)
Transformation_Details: Sequential binary partition; first ILR expresses one part vs geometric mean of remaining parts; 4 behaviors input _ 3 ILRs output; only first ILR interpreted; ILR2 & ILR3 used for regression
Closure_Method: normalized to the proportion of the total time so that the total daily time was always 24 h.
Outcome_Variable: BMI z-score, waist circumference, log fat mass index
Covariates: Age; sex; biological maturity; season of data collection; accelerometer wear time; frequency of snack food consumption in front of a screen
Time_Reallocation_Increment_minutes: 5Ð120 min modeled; main examples = ±30 min changes
Stratified_Analyses: None Ð interactions by sex and age tested but non-significant

title: The Association of the 24 Hour Distribution of Time Spent in Physical Activity, Work, and Sleep with Emotional Exhaustion.
Data Source: Primary data collection (Justus-Liebig-University Giessen, Germany)
NonWear_Criterion: Choi algorithm
WakeTime_Objective_Yes_No: Yes for MVPA; No for study time
IfWakeSubjective_questionnaire_used:
Participants answered the following two questions: ÒHow much time did you spend at university
attending lectures yesterday?Ó and ÒHow much time did you spend studying apart from attending
lecture yesterday (e.g., home exams, preparing for exams)?Ó. Participants indicated the respective
times in hours. Both values were summed up to build the factor Òstudy timeÓ.
Sleep_Detection_Method: ActiLife 6 software
Extra_Behav_Name: Self-report: "How much time did you spend at university attending lectures yesterday?" and "How much time did you spend studying apart from attending lecture yesterday (e.g., home exams, preparing for exams)?"
CoDA_Packages_Used: Physical Activity CoDa Regression Model (PACRM) developed by McGregor et al.
Closure_Method:
These proportions of
time spent in sleep, MVPA, and study were then expressed as percentages of 24 h so that their sum
(+remaining, not-considered residual) equaled 100%.
Covariates: Age; Gender

title: The Association of the Body Composition of Children with 24-Hour Activity Composition.
Data Source: Longitudinal Study of Australian Children (LSAC) - Child Health CheckPoint
NonWear_Criterion: Visual inspection of accelerometer trace + diary bed/wake times + device removal card
Sleep_Detection_Method: Visual interpretation + activity card (bedtime/wake time logs)
Cutpoint_Type: Phillips et al. 2013 cutpoints (adjusted for 50 Hz): 244, 878, 2175 g-min
Closure_Method:
Average minutes spent in each intensity
band were weighted at 5:2 for weekday and weekend days,
and linearly adjusted to collectively sum to 24 hours.
Covariates: sex; age; pubertal status; socioeconomic position

title: Use of Compositional Data Analysis to Show Estimated Changes in Cardiometabolic Health by Reallocating Time to Light-Intensity Physical Activity in Older Adults.
Data Source: Mitchelstown Cohort Rescreen Study
NonWear_Criterion: ³60 minutes of consecutive zero counts + wear diary confirmation
Sleep_Detection_Method: Calculated: time between 0500 h and the first non-sedentary epoch + time between the last non-sedentary epoch and the following 0500 h time point
LPA_Threshold:
Derived:(24h _ SB _ standing _ MVPA)
(no fixed CPM threshold)
Extra_behav_Threshold: Postural function of the monitor (A position in which one has or is maintaining an upright position while supported by one's feet)8
Transformation_Details: Default ilr transformation from the R package 'Compositions' was used.
Closure_Method: Calculated LIPA to ensure closure (LIPA = 24 h - [sedentary time + standing time + MVPA])
Outcome_Variable: BMI; body fat; fat mass; triglycerides
Covariates: Age; Sex; Disease status; Medication use; Diet; Smoking status; Alcohol consumption; Work status; Lipid markers; Glucose control markers; Fat mass

title: Compositional data analysis of 24-hour movement behaviors and mental health in workers.
Data Source: Meiji Yasuda LifeStyle (MYLS) study
NonWear_Criterion: 20 consecutive min < detection limit
NonWear_Handling: Non-wear removed; not included in behavior totals
Sleep_Detection_Method: ÒIn a typical workday/non-workday, how many hours do you usually sleep, excluding napping?Ó
Cutpoint_Type: MET thresholds from Haskell et al. (2007);  Pate et al. (2008)
Closure_Method: Remaining time allocated proportionally across SB; LPA; MVPA
Covariates: Age; Sex; BMI; Education; Economic status; Marital status; Smoking; Alcohol; Hiring status; Job type; Overtime hours

title: Compositional data analysis of 24-hour movement behaviors and mental health in workers.
Data Source: Meiji Yasuda LifeStyle (MYLS) study
NonWear_Criterion: 21 consecutive min < detection limit
NonWear_Handling: Non-wear removed; not included in behavior totals
Sleep_Detection_Method: ÒIn a typical workday/non-workday, how many hours do you usually sleep, excluding napping?Ó
Cutpoint_Type: MET thresholds from Haskell et al. (2007);  Pate et al. (2008)
Closure_Method: Sleep from self-report subtracted from 24 h; remaining time proportionally redistributed across SB, LPA, and MVPA based on their observed ratios; composition closed to 24hr
Covariates: Age; Sex; BMI; Education; Economic status; Marital status; Smoking; Alcohol; Hiring status; Job type; Overtime hours

title: Sedentary behaviour is associated with depression symptoms: Compositional data analysis from a representative sample of 3233 US adults and older adults assessed with accelerometers.
Data Source: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
NonWear_Criterion: NR
Sleep_Detection_Method: Self-reported duration (h/day)
Transformation_Details: 1st ILR = SB vs GM of LIPA+MVPA+Sleep
Covariates: Age; Sex; Ethnicity; Marital status; Income; Chronic disease; Smoking; BMI
Main_Findings: More sedentary time increased depression symptoms. Replacing SB with MVPA or sleep reduced PHQ-9 scores; replacing SB with LIPA had no effect.

title: Associations between 24 h Movement Behavior and Mental Health in Office Workers.
Data Source: Data from two different projects from the "Physical activity and healthy brain functions" research project
Day_Cycle_Definition: Wake time = diary-reported start/end of being awake; if missing, assumed 06:00Ð23:00
NonWear_Criterion: ³60 min zero counts; max 2 min of non-zero
Sleep_Detection_Method: Participants were asked to document the time when they started to try to fall asleep and out-of-bed times
Transformation_Details: Sequential binary partition; first ILR = each behavior vs geometric mean of others
Outcome_Variable: Depression symptoms; anxiety symptoms; burnout; mental wellbeing; stress
Covariates: Age;sex;education;fitness;sleep efficiency
Main_Findings: No significant associations between the 24-h movement composition and any mental health outcomes; MVPA showed a small positive association with mental wellbeing in adjusted models, but this effect disappeared after adjusting for fitness and sleep efficiency.

title: The Association Between Time-Use Behaviors and Physical and Mental Well-Being in Adults: A Compositional Isotemporal Substitution Analysis.
Data Source: Active Team RCT baseline
Day_Cycle_Definition: Individualized sleep-onset to sleep-offset (manual + diary based)
Excluded_Transition_Days: Transition periods excluded via sleep diary
NonWear_Criterion: ³60 min <25 cpm; Nonwear identified using diary timestamps when device removed at night
SleepSubjective_questionnaire_used: Sleep diary used when device not worn
Sleep_Detection_Method: Manual identification + diary
MVPA_Threshold: 403 cpm (MPA); 1131 cpm (VPA); Summed to get mvpa
Closure_Method:
Linear adjustments to 24h; Curtis et al. (2020) forced every participantÕs day to equal 24 hours. 
If the total minutes of Sleep + SB + LIPA + MVPA did not equal 1440, 
they applied small linear adjustments to each behavior so the total became exactly 24 hours.
This is different from CoDA-style closure (which scales to 1.0). 
Curtis explicitly normalized the data to 1440 minutes per day.
Covariates: Age; sex; education
Main_Findings: Time-use composition associated with BMI and physical QoL; reallocating time to MVPA predicts better outcomes; reallocating away from MVPA predicts worse outcomes.

title: Joint association between accelerometry-measured daily combination of time spent in physical activity, sedentary behaviour and sleep and all-cause mortality: a pooled analysis of six prospective cohorts using compositional analysis.
Data Source: UK Biobank
Valid_Hours_Per_Day: ³72 hours total + wear in each hour of 24h
Weighting_Scheme: Automated nonwear algorithm (<30 mg for prolonged period; mg metric)
NonWear_Criterion: Excluded
Sleep_Detection_Method: Yes
Zero_Handling_Method: log ratio EM algorithm; function lrEM of the R package zCompositions
Closure_Method:
The study did NOT fix or adjust the raw minutes to reach 1440 min/day. 
Instead, whatever numbers the study reported (even if they summed to more or less than 1440) 
were automatically converted into proportions of the total time for that person.

CoDA then closes (rescales) the values so that Sleep + SB + LIPA + MVPA = 1.0. 
This is done by dividing each behavior by the total minutes for that person.
Covariates: Age; sex; BMI; education; race; Townsend deprivation index; alcohol consumption; smoking status; self-assessed health; fruit and vegetable consumption; oily fish consumption; salt intake; red meat consumption; use of blood pressure or cholesterol medicine; physical limitations on movement; existing medical condition (cardiovascular disease; stroke; cancer); existing diagnosis of diabetes (self-reported diagnosis or use of insulin)
Main_Findings: In UK Biobank (n = 98,819), higher daily MVPA relative to sedentary and light activity was strongly associated with lower all-cause mortality. Reallocating time from SB or LIPA to MVPA substantially decreased mortality risk, whereas reallocating time from SB to LIPA had little or no protective effect. Sleep did not show a significant association with mortality in this cohort.

title: A compositional analysis of time spent in sleep, sedentary behaviour and physical activity with all-cause mortality risk.

Main_Findings: Relative MVPA reduced mortality; relative SED increased mortality; reallocating time to MVPA reduced risk and removing MVPA increased risk.

title: Balancing time use for children's fitness and adiposity: Evidence to inform 24-hour guidelines for sleep, sedentary time and physical activity.

title: Sleep and cardiometabolic health in children and adults: examining sleep as a component of the 24-h day.
Data Source: Child Health CheckPoint (LSAC)
Recruitment: National population-based LSAC cohort; assessment centres, regional mini-centres and home visits
Day_Cycle_Definition: 24-h composition of sleep, sedentary time, LPA, MVPA
NonWear_Criterion: Device removals identified from activity monitor card and visual inspection
NonWear_Handling: Non-wear for sport ²4 h imputed as MVPA; other non-wear excluded from analysis
SleepSubjective_questionnaire_used: Yes (Activity Monitor Card bed/wake times used to anchor algorithm)
Sleep_Detection_Method: van Hees sleepÐwake algorithm using 5-s epochs collapsed to 1-min; Sadeh rules for onset/offset
Zero_Handling_Method: Replaced MVPA zeros with 65% of smallest non-zero value
Transformation_Details: Four sets of three ilr coordinates; first ilr in each set represents one behaviour vs remaining behaviours
Closure_Method: Geometric means linearly adjusted so parts sum to 1440 min
Independent_Variable: 24-h activity composition ilrs (sleep, sedentary time, LPA, MVPA) and sleep characteristics
Outcome_Variable: z-BMI, SBP, DBP, MetSS, GlycA, ApoB/A1
Covariates: Sex, puberty stage, SEP, season; plus sleep timing, variability and efficiency in fully adjusted models
Main_Findings: Longer sleep duration and more MVPA within the 24-h composition were associated with better cardiometabolic profiles; reallocating time from sleep to sedentary time worsened risk, while reallocating from sedentary time or other behaviours to sleep or MVPA was generally favourable.

title: Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Associations between 24-Hour Movement Behaviours, Recreational Screen Use and Psychosocial Health Outcomes in Children: A Compositional Data Analysis Approach.

Main_Findings: Cross-sectionally, more sleep and less ST and LPA within the 24-h composition plus <=2 h/day recreational screen use were associated with better psychosocial health; no longitudinal associations observed.
